title: ai relay --json lists what each relay contract version changed
findings_note: ork integration review 2026-10-19 (R5), noted on s378
boundary: **Not in this slice:** any change to a relay rule or a contract bump, versions before 5 (the code records no change text for them), and ork's own version list.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: ork accepts a listed set of relay contract versions (ork integration review 2026-10-19, R5). To add a version on purpose, it needs to know what that version changed. Today that is recorded only as a code comment above `RELAY_CONTRACT` in `src/slicer/ai.py` (entries 5, 6 and 7). s378 put the rest of the machine-readable contract into `ai relay --json` and `ai relay-orchestrator --json` through `ai.relay_contract`; the change history is the part still missing. s382 moves the contract from v7 to v8, so this lands first and s382 adds its own entry.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/ai.py`: replace the comment entries above `RELAY_CONTRACT` with data, one `(version, text)` per version from 5 to the current one, and add it to `relay_contract`'s keys as `changes`.
- `tests/test_ai.py` or `tests/test_relay_roles.py`, next to the s378 structured-contract tests, and the s378 golden fixture `tests/fixtures/relay-contract-v7.json` if it covers the JSON.
- `docs/agents.md` (the `ai relay` and `ai relay-orchestrator` rows), `CHANGELOG.md` under Added.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_AiRelay_JsonChanges_ListsEachVersionWithText`: `ai relay --json` carries `changes`, a list of `{version, text}` in ascending order. It starts at 5, ends at `RELAY_CONTRACT`, and every `text` is one nonempty line.
- `test_AiRelayOrchestrator_JsonChanges_SameAsRelay`: `ai relay-orchestrator --json` carries the same list.
- `test_RelayContract_Bump_NeedsAChangeEntry`: the last entry's version equals `RELAY_CONTRACT`, so a bump without an entry fails.
- The texts of both commands stay byte for byte (the s378 golden tests stay green).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests; watch them go red.
2. Move the comment entries into data with the same wording, add the key, and keep a short comment that points at the data.
3. Update `docs/agents.md` and CHANGELOG.
4. Mutation-check each new test.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - `python3.12 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
